newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - January 23.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Thursday.
- The Irish government has presented a preview of its election manifesto, but little hint of its timing, with the biggest giveaway budget in the state's history.
- Business commentators criticised the Irish budget for taking risks with inflation but said it would boost the economy significantly.
- The early removal of the ban on live cattle by the Egyptian authorities is unlikely, farming sources indicated on Wednesday.

- Road blockades similar to those employed in last year's French truckers dispute have been threatened by rank-and-file trade union militants in the transport trade union CIE if the company disciplines any of the 2,500 workers who participated in Wednesday's protests.
- Irish finance minister Ruairi Quinn presented a 650 million Irish pounds general election sweetener to the country in his budget on Wednesday.
- Three police groups representing members up to the rank of superintendent have banded together to pressure the government for a pay rise.
- The controversial 'Herod Scheme' to slaughter large numbers of new-born calves to curb oversupply in the EU beef market is to be implemented in Ireland - but the number of animals will be small.

- AIB's late night announcement on Tuesday that it had made the largest acquisition in Irish corporate history to buy Dauphin Deposit Corporation of Pennsylvania won a strong endorsement from investors on Wednesday.
